Stop (115bp) and every other field unchanged.

Entry is the NYMEX BZ March 2027 (BZH7) final settlement of 6 Nov 2026, the source of every D003 mark; it is a licensed price, kept only in em-macro-data and resolved at run time (SHA-256 of 'BRENT 2027-03|2026-11-06|<settlement as %.10g>' = 36147a6bce6ca5c0a9a4b3dfe88a3424c1ccfeffa7c3b3738305c5f6fa42bbc3). The premium is repriced by the ledger's Black-76 at that close with the record's implied volatility estimate (56.4%), rate (4.03%) and expiry (2027-01-26) on 6 Nov (same commitment form for the premium = 8cfa12bc36bce8eb0adfef71dc1744e9e70f247ba936f2c9d78a73fb01b8b4e5); for this debit spread the maximum loss per unit is that premium. Spread count recomputed at the same 2% at risk of the US$10m book: 69, the most whose premium stays within US$200,000. The 6 Nov entry row (P&L 0) is kept, so P&L on the entry day is 0. Size (2%), legs, expiry, stop, horizon and every other field unchanged.

reason: Salted commitments replace the unsalted SHA-256 digests published in K002's reason. A settlement to 0.01 has only about 20,000 plausible values, so those digests can be brute-forced: treat them as disclosing the values (K002's record stays in the append-only chain unchanged). Each private value (the entry settlement, and the premium repriced at it) is now committed as SHA-256(salt || value) with its own random 32-byte salt, kept only in em-macro-data (ledger/commitments.jsonl); only the commitment is published, in the field it commits to. `python -m ledger.commitments verify` checks them with the private salts. The values are unchanged.
